significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) predictive coupling that residual-stream movement in an answer subspace—“belief-state velocity”—orders tokens by causal importance, while sustained near-zero velocity predicts safe termination better than output surprisal. This establishes both a phenomenon (low velocity marks removable reasoning and yields matched-accuracy token savings) and a proposed mechanism (useful tokens move an internal answer-relevant state), thereby fixing expectations about ablation sensitivity and stopping decisions beyond any individual token; this addresses the adaptive-compute limitation left by coarse controls such as budget forcing in s1 (Muennighoff et al., 2025). True and false are distinguishable, but the negative branch mainly rules out this velocity-based account and predictor rather than selecting a different mechanism. In the topic-substitution check, generic “mechanistic signals for efficient reasoning” would not warrant this score; the measurable velocity-to-causal-importance/convergence coupling is the claim-specific increment.

reach.justification: The transferable handle is explicitly “belief-state velocity,” used by a “training-free pruning/early-exit controller”; sustained low velocity is an ex-ante signal because it triggers answer emission before further tokens are generated, leaving an action window rather than merely explaining completed failures. Although the answer subspace requires per-model extraction, the asserted conclusion predicts what recalibration should recover—low velocity corresponds to inertness and its sustained decay to convergence—so it transfers as a relation rather than only as a search procedure. The hypothesis is framed across chain-of-thought tasks and model sizes, and its downstream users could include researchers and practitioners building latency or token-budget controls, though its dependence on an identifiable answer subspace limits applicability to less structured, open-ended reasoning. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: efficient reasoning alone supplies neither this named online quantity nor its forecast-and-stop rule.
